title: SQL analytics endpoint versus Warehouse: what compiles where
summary: The SQL analytics endpoint of a Lakehouse is read-only over its Delta tables. Compile-time metadata discovery does not enforce that. CREATE TABLE, CTAS and SELECT INTO a permanent table all compile with no result set, so a compile check cannot tell an endpoint from a Warehouse for writes. Whether a write is rejected only shows when the statement runs. Views, inline table-valued functions, procedures and reads through catalog views compile. sp_describe_first_result_set cannot describe a multi-statement batch that uses a temp table (error 11525), so describe temp-table statements one at a time. Cross-item reads use three-part names within the same workspace. Four-part (linked server) names do not exist. Identity helpers such as SCOPE_IDENTITY and @@IDENTITY are not supported.

claims.statement: Reading catalog views works the same on the endpoint and the Warehouse. sys.tables on the endpoint lists the Lakehouse Delta tables that are exposed to SQL.
claims.sql_server: Same catalog view and type in SQL Server.

claims.statement: CREATE VIEW is allowed on the read-only endpoint. Views are the normal way to add logic over Lakehouse tables.
claims.probe_sql: CREATE VIEW dbo.v_probe_endpoint AS SELECT 1 AS c

claims.statement: Inline table-valued functions can be created on the endpoint.
claims.probe_sql: CREATE FUNCTION dbo.f_probe_endpoint() RETURNS TABLE AS RETURN SELECT 1 AS c

claims.statement: Stored procedures can be created on the endpoint, provided their body only reads data or works with temp tables.
claims.probe_sql: CREATE PROCEDURE dbo.p_probe_endpoint AS SELECT 1 AS c

claims.statement: CREATE TABLE for a permanent table compiles and returns no result set. Compile-time metadata discovery does not reject it, so a compile check cannot show whether the target item is the read-only endpoint. The read-only restriction only applies when the statement runs.
claims.alternative: To create permanent tables, run the CREATE TABLE in a Warehouse of the same workspace and read the Lakehouse tables from there with three-part names.

claims.statement: CREATE TABLE AS SELECT (CTAS) is accepted Fabric syntax. It compiles and returns no result set. Compiling does not show whether the target item can store the table.
claims.probe_sql: CREATE TABLE dbo.t_probe_ctas AS SELECT 1 AS c
claims.sql_server: CTAS is not T-SQL syntax in SQL Server; use SELECT INTO there.
claims.alternative: Run the CTAS in a Warehouse when the table must persist.

claims.statement: SELECT ... INTO a permanent table compiles and returns no result set. Compiling does not show whether the write is allowed on the target item.
claims.alternative: Use SELECT INTO #temp for session-only data, or run the statement in a Warehouse.

claims.statement: sp_describe_first_result_set cannot describe a multi-statement batch that creates and then uses a local #temp table. It fails with error 11525, because metadata discovery supports temp tables only in a single-statement batch. Describe temp-table statements one at a time.
claims.probe_sql: CREATE TABLE #probe_tmp (c int); INSERT INTO #probe_tmp VALUES (1); SELECT 1 AS c
claims.sql_server: SQL Server's sp_describe_first_result_set has the same temp-table limitation.
claims.alternative: Probe each statement separately, or describe the final SELECT without the temp-table setup.

claims.statement: Global temp tables (##name) are not supported in Fabric. Code ported from SQL Server that shares ##tables between sessions fails.
claims.probe_sql: CREATE TABLE ##probe_global (c int); SELECT 1 AS c
claims.sql_server: Global temp tables work in SQL Server.
claims.alternative: Use a local #temp table, or a permanent table in a Warehouse.

claims.statement: Three-part names (item.schema.object) resolve only against Warehouses and Lakehouse endpoints in the same workspace. A name that does not match an item fails as an invalid object.
claims.sql_server: SQL Server resolves any database on the instance.
claims.alternative: Add the other item to the same workspace. For items in other workspaces, use a shortcut in the Lakehouse.

claims.statement: Four-part names (linked servers) do not exist in Fabric.
claims.sql_server: SQL Server resolves four-part names through linked servers.
claims.alternative: Use three-part names within the workspace, or OPENROWSET BULK over files.

claims.statement: SCOPE_IDENTITY is not supported in Fabric. Do not rely on the insert-then-read-identity pattern.
claims.sql_server: Returns the last identity value inserted in the current scope.
claims.alternative: Generate keys explicitly, for example with NEWID or ROW_NUMBER over the source rows.

claims.statement: @@IDENTITY is not supported in Fabric either.
claims.sql_server: Returns the last identity value inserted in the session.
claims.alternative: Generate keys explicitly with NEWID or ROW_NUMBER.

claims.statement: DB_NAME works on both and returns the item name, so it can tell code which item it is running in.
